pr_comments:
As discussed on Discord there's no guarantee the source sensor's state is available just because we receive the homeassistant start or started event.

What will work is:
- Set the utility_meter's state to `None` in the constructor
- Once the source sensor's state is available, update the state to 0 and update self._unit_of_measurement  for all tariffs

Note:
This is ONLY an issue the very first time a new `utility_meter` is added. Every time after that, the state and `unit_of_measurement` will be restored from the saved state.
As also discussed on Discord, it seems a bit over complicated to add signals for this.

Any progress on this?
Regarding @emontnemery  comment, even if the unit is updated when restored from state it's still not recognized on Grid consumption options and I can see in developer tools the tariff sensors are all with kWh unit.

A bit strange that one of the tariff's got picked up but all the others no (on my installation, on another installation no tariff's show up)
*EDIT* - Workaround is to create two new template sensors reading from the tariff's ones.

That seems to be causing another issue now though. It had no unit so now it's complaining about having a unit lol

`The unit of sensor.phase_one_nixterino (kWh) does not match the unit of already compiled statistics (None). Generation of long term statistics will be suppressed unless the unit changes back to None`
Either update existing entries in the DB with the correct spelling unit or delete all previous entries

issue_context.title: Utility meter does not assign unit of measurement with multiple tarifs
issue_context.body:
### The problem

For utility_meter with multiple tariffs unit_of_measurement is set only for the first defined tariff in table statistics_meta, which causes following errors:
Logger: homeassistant.components.sensor.recorder
Source: components/sensor/recorder.py:241
Integration: Sensor (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 13:12:02 (3 occurrences)
Last logged: 13:12:02

sensor.energy_exported_daily_g12_offpeak has unknown unit None
sensor.energy_exported_monthly_g12_offpeak has unknown unit None
sensor.energy_exported_biannually_g12_offpeak has unknown unit None

Definition of such sensor:
  energy_exported_daily_g12:
    source: sensor.se4k_m1_exported_kwh
    name: Energy Exported Daily G12
    cycle: daily
    tariffs:
      - peak
      - offpeak

statistics_meta table content:

I have had the same problem where some of the utility_meters could be used as a consumption for the energy dashboard  while others could not. The utility meter had peak and offpeak tariffs.

I had logs similar to the following lines in my logs

^[[33m2021-09-20 16:12:00 WARNING (Recorder) [homeassistant.components.sensor.recorder] The unit of sensor.ev_electricity_peak (kWh) does not match the unit of already compiled statistics (None). Generation of long term statistics will be suppressed unless the unit changes back to None^[[0m
^[[33m2021-09-20 16:12:00 WARNING (Recorder) [homeassistant.components.sensor.recorder] The unit of sensor.ev_electricity_offpeak (kWh) does not match the unit of already compiled statistics (None). Generation of long term statistics will be suppressed unless the unit changes back to None^[[0m
^[[33m2021-09-20 16:12:00 WARNING (Recorder) [homeassistant.components.sensor.recorder] sensor.daily_ev_electricity_peak has unknown unit None^[[0m
^[[33m2021-09-20 16:12:00 WARNING (Recorder) [homeassistant.components.sensor.recorder] sensor.weekly_ev_electricity_peak has unknown unit None^[[0m
^[[33m2021-09-20 16:12:00 WARNING (Recorder) [homeassistant.components.sensor.recorder] The unit of sensor.monthly_ev_electricity_peak (kWh) does not match the unit of already compiled statistics (None). Generation of long term statistics will be suppressed unless the unit changes back to None^[[0m
^[[33m2021-09-20 16:12:00 WARNING (Recorder) [homeassistant.components.sensor.recorder] The unit of sensor.monthly_ev_electricity_offpeak (kWh) does not match the unit of already compiled statistics (None). Generation of long term statistics will be suppressed unless the unit changes back to None^[[0m

I opened the sqllite database and fixed the unit_of_measurement for all these entities which fixed my problem. I could see the info again in the energy dashboard.


cd /config 
sqlite3 home-assistant_v2.db

and the sqls similar to 
update statistics_meta set unit_of_measurement="kWh" WHERE statistic_id="sensor.monthly_ev_electricity_offpeak";

After fixing the units for each of the sensor entities, this is working as intended again for me.

review_comments: Please use our dispatch helper to signal the entity instead of storing the entities in a shared container. Accessing entities from outside is fragile.

Such a solution was implemented previously in this PR, I think it's @dgomes may have force-pushed so it's no longer visible. Doing it via signaling instead introduces a race which we must then guard against and the whole things becomes over complicated.

I think this is a better, or at least good enough, solution in this case, the children entities of a utility_meter can't change unless the configuration is changed and the utility_meter is reloaded.

The race is that the utility meter's sub sensors may race against each other.

Let's say we have a utility_meter with two tariffs, `sensor.tarif_1` and `sensor.tarif_2`, based on sensor `sensor.energy_meter`

1. `sensor.energy_meter` has a state update, `unit_of_measurement` = "kWh"
2. `sensor.tariff_1 gets` its initial state and resets itself with `unit_of_measurement = kW`h + dispatches a signal for the other entities to also reset
3. `sensor.energy_meter` has a state update, `unit_of_measurement = "rabbits"`
4. tariff is changed, `sensor.tariff_2` gets its initial state and resets itself with `unit_of_measurement = "rabbits` + dispatches a signal for the other entities to also reset
5. `sensor.tariff_2` receives the reset signal from `sensor.tariff_1`
6. `sensor.tariff_1` receives the reset signal from `sensor.tariff_2`

The example is maybe not realistic, but the race is there.

It looks like the problem lies in the source of the signal instead of the fact that we're using signals. Why does one entity cause other entities to reset? I'd expect there to be a separate coordinator that decides this.

Before this PR:
- `utility_meter` set its state to 0, with no `unit_of_measurement` and no `device_class` when initialized
- when receiving an initial valid state from the source sensor, the `unit_of_measurement` and `device_class` are both updated according with the source sensor's `unit_of_measurement` and `device_class`

This behavior was not wanted, because 0 is a perfectly valid state, but the `unit_of_measurement` and `device_class` were not yet known.

With this PR, we wait for a valid state from the source sensor before initializing the utility_meter's state to 0 and setting `device_class` and `unit_of_measurement`

What makes it slightly complicated is that one utility_meter may create multiple sensors for different tariffs, all based on the same source sensor.

Right. I'm saying I think we can avoid the race if we move the coordination of resetting or updating the sensors for the same source to a separate single coordinator. It's possible I'm missing some detail why that's not possible.

The requirement to have the `unit_of_measurement` always set led to these developments, previously the tariff sensor would get its `unit_of_measurement` set whenever it started collecting independently. There was no need for any coordination (and therefore non existed)

This current patch provides IMHO such coordination because each sensor can share it's `unit_of_measurement` with the remaining sensors.

There is added benefit: the utility_meter can now track all it's child sensors, if I need to sum all the tariffs I can programatically get all child tariffs from the utility_meter (that will be a future PR).

> we can avoid the race if we move the coordination of resetting or updating the sensors for the same source to a separate single coordinator.

Now I understand what you mean Martin! That would indeed be a nicer solution; the utility_meter parent tracks the source sensor and updates its children.
